title: Gift deed vs sale deed - the tax and legal implications
p1:
Giving away property and selling property may look like two different ways of transferring ownership. But the choice can create very different legal and tax outcomes.

Many people assume a gift deed is always cheaper because no money changes hands. That is not always true.
p2:
A gift deed transfers property voluntarily without payment, usually to someone close. A sale deed involves payment and creates a buyer-seller relationship. The surprising part? A gift may still have tax implications depending on who receives it and the value of the property.

Also, a properly executed gift deed can affect future ownership rights, just like a sale deed.
p3:
The right choice depends on factors like family relationship, stamp duty, tax rules, and future plans for the property. A decision made only to save immediate costs can create complications later.

Before transferring property, look beyond the registration fee. The document you choose can impact ownership, taxes, and future disputes.
conclusion: If you had to transfer property to a family member, would you choose a gift deed or a sale deed? What factor would influence your decision most?
